title: Building a Custom Inference App (Android) 📱
description: Walk through the full Android app code to load a TFLite model, process input, run inference, and display results.

slides.title: From .tflite to Android APK 🤖
slides.content:
# Step‑by‑Step

1. Add TFLite dependency to `build.gradle`.
2. Place the .tflite file in `app/src/main/assets/`.
3. Create a helper class to load model and run inference.
4. Preprocess camera/image input into the format the model expects.
5. Postprocess output tensors into human‑readable results.

We'll build a simple digit recognizer using a MNIST CNN.

slides.content: Add TensorFlow Lite and optionally support library.

quizData.explanation: The assets folder is the standard location for raw files that are bundled with the APK.

slides.title: Load Model and Define Inference 🔍
slides.content:
# Interpreter Setup (Kotlin)

```kotlin
private lateinit var interpreter: Interpreter

private fun loadModelFile(): ByteBuffer {
    val assetFileDescriptor = assets.openFd("mnist_model.tflite")
    val inputStream = FileInputStream(assetFileDescriptor.fileDescriptor)
    val fileChannel = inputStream.channel
    val startOffset = assetFileDescriptor.startOffset
    val declaredLength = assetFileDescriptor.declaredLength
    return fileChannel.map(FileChannel.MapMode.READ_ONLY, startOffset, declaredLength)
}

interpreter = Interpreter(loadModelFile())
```

slides.title: Memory Mapping for Speed 💨
slides.content: Use `MappedByteBuffer` as shown above – it loads the model lazily and shares memory, reducing RAM usage.
